in_hebrew.name: חניכה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A woman whose name means 'gracious' or 'merciful'. Derived from the Hebrew root חנך (חנך, chanak), meaning 'to educate, to train'. This name is a compound of the Hebrew words חנך (hanak) and רך (rik), meaning 'grace' and 'strength' or 'might', respectively. Thus, the name Heinrike can be translated as 'gracious strength' or 'merciful might'. The name is also found in the Bible as 'Hannah' (1 Samuel 1:1-28), who was a barren woman who prayed to God for a child and was eventually blessed with a son named Samuel.

in_greek.name: Ειρήνη
in_greek.long_meaning: A Greek name derived from the word ειρήνη (eirēnē), meaning 'peace'. This name was popular among the ancient Greeks as a symbol of peace and tranquility. It is also the name of the Greek goddess of peace, Eirene. The name Heinrike may be derived from the Greek name Eirene, as the German name Heike or Heidrun is believed to be derived from the Old Norse name Hjördís, which is also derived from the Old Norse word hjör, meaning 'peace'. Thus, the name Heinrike can be seen as a fusion of the German and Greek traditions, representing both 'gracious strength' and 'peace'.

in_latin.name: Hilaria
in_latin.long_meaning: A Latin name derived from the word hilaris, meaning 'cheerful' or 'joyful'. This name was used in ancient Rome to describe a happy and lively person.
